questions.question_english: Which of the following instructional methodologies is traditionally most dominant in a subject-centered curriculum?
options_english: Expository teaching (such as the lecture method)
Guided inquiry-based and discovery learning
Collaborative role-playing and simulations
Peer-led interactive brainstorming sessions
questions.explanation_english: In a traditional subject-centered curriculum, the predominant instructional strategy is expository teaching, most commonly manifested as direct instruction and the lecture method. Because subject-centered design treats knowledge as a pre-existing, codified body of facts, concepts, and principles structured by academic disciplines, the teacher assumes the role of the primary knowledge authority and dispenser of information. The pedagogical objective is systematic, sequential, and efficient content coverage. Consequently, students primarily function as receptive listeners, note-takers, and absorbers of textbook material. In contrast, inquiry-based learning, simulations, and brainstorming are constructivist, student-centered pedagogies that emphasize experiential discovery, active dialogue, and collaborative problem-solving.
questions.explanation_hindi: पारंपरिक विषय-केंद्रित पाठ्यचर्या में सबसे प्रमुख शिक्षण रणनीति व्याख्यात्मक शिक्षण (Expository teaching) है, जिसका सबसे सामान्य रूप व्याख्यान विधि (Lecture method) और प्रत्यक्ष अनुदेशन है। चूंकि इस प्रारूप में ज्ञान को पहले से स्थापित तथ्यों, नियमों और सिद्धांतों के एक संरचित निकाय के रूप में देखा जाता है, इसलिए शिक्षक कक्षा में ज्ञान के सर्वोच्च स्रोत एवं विशेषज्ञ के रूप में कार्य करता है। शिक्षण का मुख्य लक्ष्य निश्चित समय-सीमा के भीतर विषय-वस्तु को व्यवस्थित रूप से समाप्त करना होता है। इसके परिणामस्वरूप, छात्र मुख्य रूप से निष्क्रिय श्रोता, नोट्स लेने वाले और पाठ्यपुस्तक अभ्यासों को हल करने वाले बनकर रह जाते हैं। इसके विपरीत, पूछताछ-आधारित अधिगम, भूमिका-निर्वाह और विचार-मंथन जैसी विधियाँ रचनावादी और शिक्षार्थी-केंद्रित दृष्टिकोण से जुड़ी हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Expository teaching (Lecture method)

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Traditional subject-centered curricula rely heavily on expository teaching methodologies, primarily the lecture method. In this teacher-dominated approach, the instructor acts as the primary knowledge authority who systematically presents structured factual content, concepts, and principles to students, while learners mainly listen, take notes, and complete standard textbook exercises.

questions.question_english: If a curriculum planner selects subject matter based on the criterion of 'Utility', they are prioritizing:

Content that is structurally simplest to assess objectively through standardized multiple-choice items
Content that primarily appeals to the subjective aesthetic appreciation and artistic tastes of learners

questions.explanation_english: Prioritizing 'Utility' in curriculum content selection focuses on knowledge, capabilities, and values that have practical application in the learner's immediate and future life. Derived from pragmatic educational philosophy (such as John Dewey's experientialism and Herbert Spencer's query 'What Knowledge is of Most Worth?'), utility ensures that curriculum content equips students to resolve functional real-world problems, navigate civic responsibilities, secure meaningful livelihoods, and maintain personal well-being.
questions.explanation_hindi: विषय-वस्तु चयन में 'उपयोगिता' (Utility) के मानदंड को प्राथमिकता देने का सीधा अर्थ है ऐसी विषय-वस्तु का चयन करना जो विद्यार्थियों के वर्तमान और भविष्य के वास्तविक जीवन की समस्याओं, चुनौतियों और आवश्यकताओं को हल करने में सक्षम हो। यह उपागम जॉन डीवी के प्रयोजनवाद और हर्बर्ट स्पेंसर के उपयोगितावादी दर्शन से प्रेरित है, जिसका मानना है कि विद्यालयी ज्ञान केवल अमूर्त या सैद्धांतिक न होकर व्यावहारिक जीवन, सामाजिक दायित्वों, आजीविका और व्यक्तिगत आत्मनिर्भरता में प्रत्यक्ष रूप से उपयोगी होना चाहिए।

questions.question_english: Which educational philosopher is most prominently associated with the philosophical advocacy of a child-centered curriculum and experiential 'learning by doing'?
options_english: John Locke
John Dewey
Ivan Pavlov
B.F. Skinner
questions.explanation_english: John Dewey (1859–1952), the foremost American philosopher of Pragmatism and Progressive Education, is globally renowned for advocating a child-centered curriculum rooted in experiential learning ('learning by doing'). Dewey argued in seminal works like 'Democracy and Education' and 'The School and Society' that education is not merely a preparation for future living, but life itself. He emphasized reflective inquiry, collaborative problem-solving, democratic classrooms, and connecting learning directly to the child’s daily social experiences. In contrast, John Locke proposed the 'tabula rasa' (blank slate), while Pavlov and Skinner were behaviorists focused on conditioning rather than child-centered experiential philosophy.
questions.explanation_hindi: जॉन डीवी (John Dewey, 1859–1952) प्रयोजनवाद (Pragmatism) और प्रगतिशील शिक्षा के अग्रणी दार्शनिक हैं, जिन्हें बाल-केंद्रित पाठ्यक्रम और 'करके सीखने' (Learning by Doing) के विचार का प्रमुख प्रस्तावक माना जाता है। डीवी ने 'डेमोक्रेसी एंड एजुकेशन' और 'द स्कूल एंड सोसाइटी' जैसी कृतियों में स्पष्ट किया कि शिक्षा भावी जीवन की तैयारी मात्र नहीं, बल्कि स्वयं जीवन है। उन्होंने लोकतांत्रिक कक्षा परिवेश, समस्या-समाधान, चिंतनशील अधिगम और बालक के वास्तविक सामाजिक अनुभवों के पुनर्गठन पर बल दिया। इसके विपरीत, जॉन लॉक ने 'तबुला रासा' (कोरी स्लेट) का विचार दिया था, जबकि पावलोव और स्किनर व्यवहारवादी मनोवैज्ञानिक थे।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) John Dewey

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: John Dewey, a leading philosopher of Pragmatism and Progressive Education, strongly advocated for a child-centered curriculum rooted in experiential learning. He argued that education should be life itself, not merely preparation for future living. Dewey emphasized hands-on problem solving, democratic classroom environments, reflective thinking, and connecting learning directly to the child’s daily social experiences.

questions.question_english: What role do 'Hub and Spoke' models play in skill-based curriculum integration at the school level?
options_english: Administrative frameworks utilized to penalize schools demonstrating poor academic test results
A centralized logistical model for distributing daily nutritional midday meals across schools
System planning models that dictate daily school bus routes for regional student transportation
Well-equipped Hub schools share vocational resources with neighboring Spoke schools
questions.explanation_english: The 'Hub and Spoke' model in skill-based curriculum delivery optimizes resource allocation and cost efficiency. Well-equipped central 'Hub' schools—possessing advanced vocational workshops, specialized technical tools, and certified expert trainers—share their infrastructure, equipment, and master classes with nearby 'Spoke' schools. This collaborative arrangement ensures equitable access to high-quality skill and vocational training for all students across a school complex without requiring expensive, duplicative capital expenditures in every institution.
questions.explanation_hindi: प्रत्येक व्यक्तिगत विद्यालय में उन्नत व्यावसायिक प्रयोगशालाएं (जैसे रोबोटिक्स लैब, आधुनिक कार्यशालाएं, ऑटोमोबाइल एवं इलेक्ट्रॉनिक्स टूल्स) स्थापित करना अत्यधिक खर्चीला और आर्थिक रूप से अव्यावहारिक होता है। इस अवसंरचनात्मक चुनौती से निपटने के लिए शैक्षणिक प्रशासन 'हब एंड स्पोक' (Hub and Spoke) मॉडल का उपयोग करता है। इस मॉडल के अंतर्गत, एक केंद्रीय सर्वसुविधायुक्त विद्यालय को 'हब' (Hub) बनाया जाता है, जहाँ अत्याधुनिक उपकरण, कार्यशालाएं और विशेषज्ञ प्रशिक्षक उपलब्ध होते हैं। इसके चारों ओर स्थित अन्य सामान्य विद्यालय 'स्पोक' (Spoke) कहलाते हैं। स्पोक विद्यालयों के विद्यार्थी निश्चित दिनों में हब स्कूल में जाकर प्रायोगिक कौशल प्रशिक्षण प्राप्त करते हैं या हब से संसाधन साझा किए जाते हैं। यह प्रशासनिक व्यवस्था वित्तीय संसाधनों का अनुकूलतम उपयोग करती है और सभी विद्यार्थियों को समान गुणवत्तापूर्ण कौशल प्रशिक्षण सुलभ कराती है।

questions.question_english: In the SMART criteria framework for setting sound educational and instructional objectives, the letter 'M' stands for:
options_english: Meaningful
Manageable
Motivational
Measurable
questions.explanation_english: In the SMART goal-setting framework widely utilized in curriculum design and pedagogy, 'M' stands for Measurable. The complete SMART acronym represents: Specific (explicit and clear target), Measurable (quantifiable or observable evidence of attainment), Achievable/Attainable (realistic within learner capacity), Relevant (aligned with curricular aims and life needs), and Time-bound (framed within a specified duration). Measurability guarantees that educators can objectively assess whether and to what standard the intended learning outcome has been mastered.
questions.explanation_hindi: पाठ्यचर्या अभिकल्पन और शैक्षिक प्रबंधन में प्रयुक्त 'SMART' ढांचे में 'M' का अर्थ 'मापने योग्य' (Measurable) होता है। SMART का पूर्ण रूप है: S - Specific (विशिष्ट), M - Measurable (मापने योग्य/मापनीय), A - Achievable (प्राप्य/साध्य), R - Relevant (प्रासंगिक), और T - Time-bound (समयबद्ध)। उद्देश्यों की मापनीयता यह सुनिश्चित करती है कि शिक्षक स्पष्ट मूल्यांकन उपकरणों (जैसे रूब्रिक्स, परीक्षण) के माध्यम से वस्तुनिष्ठ रूप से यह जांच सकें कि विद्यार्थी ने लक्षित ज्ञान या कौशल किस सीमा तक अर्जित किया है।

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: In the SMART framework for objective setting, ‘M’ stands for Measurable. Educational objectives must be formulated using precise action verbs so that student achievement can be quantitatively or qualitatively evaluated. Measurability allows educators to determine objectively whether the target learning outcomes have been attained following instruction.

questions.question_english: From the perspective of institutional school leadership, which of the following represents a primary structural and administrative barrier to implementing an integrated curriculum in secondary schools?
options_english: Rigid timetable scheduling constraints and entrenched departmental silos
A widespread intrinsic lack of student interest in real-world multifaceted problems
Excessive financial procurement costs associated with purchasing commercial integrated textbooks
Statutory legal prohibitions against cross-curricular teaching enacted under national education acts
questions.explanation_english: In secondary education, the greatest organizational obstacle to curriculum integration is the entrenched structural architecture of secondary schools—specifically, rigid period-based timetables and siloed academic departments. Secondary schools are historically organized around specialized disciplines (e.g., Department of Physics, Department of History) with fixed 40-to-45-minute periods and separate subject-specific certification requirements for teachers. This administrative compartmentalization severely restricts the flexibility needed for interdisciplinary co-teaching, block scheduling, thematic inquiry, and joint planning time. Educational administrators must actively introduce structural innovations, such as block scheduling and professional learning communities (PLCs), to dismantle these silos.
questions.explanation_hindi: माध्यमिक स्तर पर एकीकृत पाठ्यचर्या को लागू करने में सबसे बड़ी प्रशासनिक व संस्थागत बाधा माध्यमिक विद्यालयों का पारंपरिक ढांचा है—अर्थात 40-45 मिनट के निश्चित कालांशों वाली कठोर समय-सारणी और अलग-थलग विषय विभाग (Departmental Silos)। माध्यमिक विद्यालयों में शिक्षक विशिष्ट विषयों (जैसे भौतिकी, रसायन, इतिहास) के विशेषज्ञ के रूप में नियुक्त होते हैं और अपने-अपने विभागों में ही सीमित रहते हैं। यह ढांचा शिक्षकों को संयुक्त रूप से पढ़ाने, बड़े समय-ब्लॉक (Block Scheduling) में प्रोजेक्ट्स कराने और मिलकर योजना बनाने की प्रशासनिक अनुमति नहीं देता। जब तक विद्यालय प्राचार्य समय-सारणी में लचीलापन नहीं लाते और अंतर्विभागीय संवाद को संस्थागत रूप नहीं देते, तब तक इस बाधा को पार करना अत्यंत कठिन होता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Timetable scheduling and departmental silos.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: A major administrative challenge in secondary schools is overcoming rigid timetable structures and entrenched departmental silos. questions.question_english: According to the National Education Policy 2020, the new curricular and pedagogical structure of school education is:
questions.explanation_english: NEP 2020 replaced the erstwhile 10+2 structure (which only covered ages 6 to 18) with a comprehensive 5+3+3+4 curricular and pedagogical model covering ages 3 to 18. This model reflects children's cognitive and psychological developmental milestones through four distinct stages: (1) Foundational Stage (5 years, ages 3–8: 3 years ECCE + Grades 1-2); (2) Preparatory Stage (3 years, ages 8–11: Grades 3-5); (3) Middle Stage (3 years, ages 11–14: Grades 6-8); and (4) Secondary Stage (4 years, ages 14–18: Grades 9-12 with multidisciplinary choice). Bringing early childhood education (ages 3–6) into the formal educational framework is a landmark achievement of this restructuring.
questions.explanation_hindi: राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति (NEP) 2020 ने पुरानी 10+2 प्रणाली को समाप्त करके बच्चों के संज्ञानात्मक विकास के चरणों के अनुकूल एक नई '5+3+3+4' पाठ्यचर्या और शैक्षणिक संरचना प्रस्तुत की है, जो 3 से 18 वर्ष के आयु वर्ग को समाहित करती है। इस संरचना के चार मुख्य चरण हैं: (1) बुनियादी चरण (Foundational Stage): 5 वर्ष (आयु 3-8 वर्ष, प्री-स्कूल से कक्षा 2); (2) तैयारी/प्रारंभिक चरण (Preparatory Stage): 3 वर्ष (आयु 8-11 वर्ष, कक्षा 3-5); (3) मध्य चरण (Middle Stage): 3 वर्ष (आयु 11-14 वर्ष, कक्षा 6-8); और (4) माध्यमिक चरण (Secondary Stage): 4 वर्ष (आयु 14-18 वर्ष, कक्षा 9-12 बहुविषयक अध्ययन सहित)। इस संरचना का सबसे ऐतिहासिक पहलू 3 से 6 वर्ष की प्रारंभिक बाल्यावस्था देखभाल एवं शिक्षा (ECCE) को औपचारिक स्कूली ढांचे में शामिल करना है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) 5 + 3 + 3 + 4

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: National Education Policy 2020 replaced the old 10+2 system with a new 5+3+3+4 curricular structure. This design covers ages 3 to 18 through four distinct stages: 5 years of Foundational Stage (ages 3-8), 3 years of Preparatory Stage (ages 8-11), 3 years of Middle Stage (ages 11-14), and 4 years of Secondary Stage (ages 14-18).

questions.question_english: In curriculum planning and educational needs analysis, the concept of 'felt needs' refers to:
options_english: Top-down administrative mandates identified exclusively by senior educational planners
Mandatory statutory requirements and legal regulations imposed by the state
Deep latent unconscious psychological drives and developmental impulses of students
Needs consciously recognized and articulated directly by the learners themselves
questions.explanation_english: In educational theory and social planning (notably articulated in Jonathan Bradshaw's typology of social needs), 'felt needs' represent the desires, goals, and learning deficits that are consciously recognized and articulated by the learners themselves. Unlike normative needs (which are dictated from above by experts against an established standard), felt needs reflect the learner's own self-perceived interests and challenges. Incorporating felt needs into curriculum development promotes intrinsic learner motivation, student-centeredness, and emotional investment in the educational journey.
questions.explanation_hindi: पाठ्यचर्या नियोजन और शैक्षिक समाजशास्त्र (जैसे ब्रैडशॉ का आवश्यकता वर्गीकरण) में 'अनुभूत आवश्यकताएं' (Felt Needs) वे आवश्यकताएं, आकांक्षाएं या कमियां हैं जिन्हें शिक्षार्थी स्वयं सचेत रूप से महसूस करते हैं और प्रत्यक्ष रूप से व्यक्त करते हैं। यह विशेषज्ञों द्वारा ऊपर से थोपे गए मानकों (मानक आवश्यकताओं) से भिन्न होती हैं। पाठ्यचर्या निर्माण में विद्यार्थियों की अनुभूत आवश्यकताओं को स्थान देने से शिक्षण-अधिगम प्रक्रिया छात्र-केंद्रित बनती है और शिक्षार्थियों की आंतरिक अभिप्रेरणा व सहभागिता में अत्यधिक वृद्धि होती है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Needs consciously recognized and expressed by learners themselves.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Felt needs refer to requirements, desires, or gaps consciously recognized and directly expressed by the learners themselves. Recognizing felt needs in curriculum planning ensures that student voices, personal interests, and self-identified learning goals are incorporated, which enhances student engagement, intrinsic motivation, and personal investment in the educational process.

questions.question_english: Under modern continuous and holistic assessment frameworks, the evaluation of co-curricular activities is most appropriately recorded and reported through:

Binary qualitative pass/fail declarations without diagnostic feedback
Competitive numerical rank orders and inter-student percentile distributions

Consider the following principles of curriculum construction:
I. Principle of Forward-Looking
II. Principle of Creative Experience
III. Principle of Conservation
IV. Principle of Rigid Standardisation
Which of the principles listed above are generally accepted as sound principles of curriculum construction?

I, III and IV only
II, III and IV only

questions.explanation_english:
Sound curriculum construction relies on three core principles among those listed:
- Principle of Forward-Looking (I): Preparing learners for future societal, technological, and vocational transformations rather than confining them to the past.
- Principle of Creative Experience (II): Providing avenues for creative self-expression, discovery, active inquiry, and constructivist problem-solving.
- Principle of Conservation (III): Preserving and transmitting essential cultural heritage, historical wisdom, and foundational moral values to the new generation.
Conversely, 'Rigid Standardization' (IV) violates the fundamental educational tenets of flexibility, learner-centeredness, and pedagogical differentiation required to cater to individual differences. Thus, only I, II, and III are valid principles.

इसके विपरीत, 'कठोर मानकीकरण' (IV) एक अमान्य और नकारात्मक दृष्टिकोण है, क्योंकि पाठ्यक्रम को लचीला और शिक्षार्थियों की व्यक्तिगत भिन्नताओं तथा विविध आवश्यकताओं के अनुकूल होना चाहिए। अतः विकल्प (A) केवल I, II और III सही है।

questions.question_english: Which of the following curriculum designs is most closely aligned with the educational philosophies of 'Perennialism' and 'Essentialism'?
options_english: Learner-centered curriculum
Subject-centered curriculum
Problem-centered curriculum
Experience-centered curriculum
questions.explanation_english: A subject-centered curriculum design organizes the educational program around distinct, traditional academic disciplines (such as mathematics, history, natural science, and literature) and is deeply grounded in the philosophies of Essentialism and Perennialism. Essentialism, championed by educational thinkers like William Bagley, emphasizes the mastery of foundational academic skills (the 3 Rs), core factual knowledge, and cultural heritage deemed indispensable for maintaining civilized society. Perennialism, articulated by philosophers like Robert Maynard Hutchins and Mortimer Adler, asserts that human nature remains constant across time and that education should focus on universal, enduring truths and the classical disciplines. Both philosophies prioritize intellectual discipline, structured disciplinary logic, academic rigor, and teacher-directed expository pedagogy over student-selected, interest-driven activities. In contrast, learner-centered and experience-centered designs derive from Progressivism (John Dewey), while problem-centered designs reflect Reconstructionism.
questions.explanation_hindi: विषय-केंद्रित पाठ्यचर्या प्रारूप (Subject-centered curriculum design) शैक्षिक कार्यक्रम को विशिष्ट, पारंपरिक शैक्षणिक विषयों (जैसे गणित, इतिहास, विज्ञान और साहित्य) के आधार पर व्यवस्थित करता है और यह मुख्य रूप से 'शाश्वतवाद' (Perennialism) और 'सारतत्ववाद/आवश्यकतावाद' (Essentialism) के दर्शन पर आधारित है। विलियम बैगले जैसे विचारकों द्वारा समर्थित सारतत्ववाद, समाज के संरक्षण और निरंतरता के लिए बुनियादी शैक्षणिक कौशलों (3 Rs), अनिवार्य तथ्यों और सांस्कृतिक विरासत के संचरण पर बल देता है। वहीं, रॉबर्ट मेनार्ड हचिन्स और मोर्टिमर एडलर द्वारा समर्थित शाश्वतवाद यह मानता है कि मानवीय प्रकृति सर्वकालिक और स्थिर है, अतः शिक्षा का केंद्र चिरंतन सत्य, शाश्वत विचार और बौद्धिक अनुशासन होना चाहिए। ये दोनों दर्शन विषय-सामग्री की सुदृढ़ संरचना, बौद्धिक कठोरता और शिक्षक-निर्देशित अनुदेशन का समर्थन करते हैं। इसके विपरीत, शिक्षार्थी-केंद्रित और अनुभव-केंद्रित प्रारूप 'प्रगतिवाद' (जॉन डीवी) से तथा समस्या-केंद्रित प्रारूप 'पुनर्निर्माणवाद' से संबंधित हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Subject-centered curriculum

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The subject-centered curriculum aligns closely with Essentialism and Perennialism. Essentialism advocates teaching core academic subjects and fundamental skills necessary for societal preservation, while Perennialism emphasizes enduring ideas and timeless truths found in classic literature and established disciplines. Both philosophies prioritize structured discipline knowledge, intellectual rigor, and teacher-directed instruction.

questions.question_english: A key pedagogical approach advocated by NCF-FS for early childhood education is:
options_english: Heavy institutional reliance on formal textbooks and written paper assignments
Mechanical rote memorisation of alphabetic scripts and basic numerical tables
Enforcing strict disciplinary classroom routines and total student silence
Play-based, inquiry-based, and activity-based learning.
questions.explanation_english: NCF-FS 2022 underscores that play is the most natural, developmentally appropriate, and powerful vehicle through which young children learn and make sense of their world. The curriculum framework explicitly moves away from formal, textbook-heavy instruction, rote memorization, and strict seated discipline. Instead, it mandates a rich blend of play-based (free play and guided play), inquiry-based (asking questions, exploring natural phenomena), and activity-based learning (manipulating concrete objects, storytelling, puppetry, music, movement, and arts). This approach fosters cognitive flexibility, executive functioning, socio-emotional competence, and an intrinsic joy of learning.
questions.explanation_hindi: NCF-FS 2022 इस बात पर विशेष बल देता है कि खेल छोटे बच्चों के स्वाभाविक विकास और सीखने का सबसे प्रभावी माध्यम है। यह पाठ्यचर्या औपचारिक पाठ्यपुस्तकों, यांत्रिक रटन प्रणाली और कठोर कक्षा अनुशासन से हटकर खेल-आधारित, अन्वेषण-आधारित और गतिविधि-आधारित शिक्षाशास्त्र को अनिवार्य बनाती है। छोटे बच्चे सक्रिय रूप से वस्तुओं को छूकर, खेल खेलकर, कहानियां सुनकर, कठपुतली, संगीत, चित्रकला और संवाद के माध्यम से सीखते हैं। यह बाल-केंद्रित दृष्टिकोण बच्चों में संज्ञानात्मक विकास, जिज्ञासा, समस्या-समाधान कौशल और सीखने के प्रति स्वाभाविक उत्साह विकसित करता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Play-based, inquiry-based, and activity-based learning.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: NCF-FS emphasizes that early pedagogy must be play-based, inquiry-based, and activity-oriented. Young children construct knowledge through physical movement, storytelling, art, music, sensory exploration, and interactive games. Formal, textbook-centric instruction and rigid drill exercises are discouraged, as play provides the most natural, effective medium for early childhood development.

questions.question_english: Hilda Taba modified Tyler’s model by introducing the 'Grassroots approach'. How does Taba’s model differ fundamentally from Tyler’s?
options_english: Taba asserted that curriculum frameworks must be designed top-down exclusively by external ministry experts
Taba systematically removed all quantitative and qualitative evaluation mechanisms from the development process
Taba completely replaced learning objectives with administrative resource budgeting and financial targets
By advocating teacher-led bottom-up design starting with instructional units
questions.explanation_english: Hilda Taba modified Tyler's deductive, top-down administrative model by proposing an inductive 'Grassroots Approach' in her 1962 work 'Curriculum Development: Theory and Practice'. Taba believed that curriculum should be designed by the users of the program—namely, classroom teachers who directly work with learners. Rather than having distant educational administrators hand down global curriculum directives, Taba's model is bottom-up: teachers diagnose student needs, design specific instructional learning units inductively, test and refine them in authentic classrooms, and subsequently generalize and weave them into broader curricular frameworks. Hence, Option D is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: जहाँ राल्फ टायलर का मॉडल एक शीर्ष से नीचे (Top-down) प्रशासनिक उपागम था (जिसमें पाठ्यचर्या का निर्धारण प्रशासकों व केंद्रीय समितियों द्वारा किया जाता था और शिक्षकों को केवल उसे लागू करना होता था), वहीं हिल्डा ताबा (Hilda Taba) ने 1962 में अपनी पुस्तक 'करिकुलम डेवलपमेंट: थ्योरी एंड प्रैक्टिस' में एक आगमनात्मक 'जमीनी उपागम' (Grassroots Approach) प्रस्तावित किया। ताबा का दृढ़ विश्वास था कि जो शिक्षक विद्यार्थियों को पढ़ाते हैं, उन्हीं को पाठ्यचर्या के निर्माण में मुख्य भूमिका निभानी चाहिए। उनका नीचे से ऊपर (Bottom-up) मॉडल शिक्षकों द्वारा शिक्षार्थियों की आवश्यकताओं का निदान करने, कक्षा स्तर पर विशिष्ट प्रायोगिक शिक्षण इकाइयों (Instructional Units) को विकसित, परीक्षित और परिष्कृत करने से प्रारंभ होता है। इसलिए विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) By advocating teacher-led bottom-up design starting with instructional units.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Hilda Taba modified Tyler’s top-down approach by advocating a grassroots, teacher-led bottom-up model. She asserted that teachers, who work directly with students, should design curriculum starting by creating, testing, and refining specific teaching-learning units in classrooms before inducting them into generalized national or regional curriculum structures.
